options.how: You play a dynasty across centuries, managing a realm, vassals and heirs on a map of medieval Europe and beyond.
Command a few squads on one battlefield, using cover and capturing territory points.

sources.note: Crusader Kings III: Steam: released Sep 1 2020; bloodline continues through heirs, vassals and titles, map from Nordic lands/Africa to China and Japan
Company of Heroes: review: squads as units, fighting from cover

options.how: Three mechs on an 8x8 grid; every enemy attack is telegraphed for one turn.
Run a nation from 1444 to 1821 on a world map of provinces, trade and colonization.

sources.note: Into the Breach: Steam: released Feb 27 2018; 'All enemy attacks are telegraphed'; 3 mechs and 8x8 grid not stated on page
Europa Universalis IV: Steam: released Aug 13 2013; four centuries from late Middle Ages to Napoleonic era, trade power in provinces, colonize New World

options.how: Each mission is one battle on a single grid map, building units from captured factories, with no empire layer.

options.game: Master of Orion II: Battle at Antares
options.how: Colonize and govern a galaxy of star systems, research tech and wage interstellar war.

sources.note: Advance Wars: official page
Master of Orion II: Battle at Antares: GOG: 1996 release; colonize planets, 60 technology fields, take over alien star systems, tactical ship combat

options.how: Plan a few soldiers' moves simultaneously in a small procedural building, then watch the turn resolve.
Control a nation's industry, divisions and fronts across WWII.

sources.note: Frozen Synapse: Steam: released May 26 2011; plan squad actions, both sides' turns execute simultaneously; random generation plus hand-crafted levels
Hearts of Iron IV: Steam: released Jun 6 2016; guide a nation through WWII, manage industry/factories, design division templates

options.how: Each battle is a small map with a few mechs, and every enemy attack is telegraphed a turn ahead.
Found and grow a faction across an alien planet with bases, research and diplomacy.

sources.note: Into the Breach: mechs on small maps; all enemy attacks are telegraphed
Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri: GOG: original 1999; seven factions on planet Chiron, exhaustive tech tree, complex diplomacy, colonies

options.how: A three-hero team fights turn-based on small maps with cover and team moves.
Guide a civilization from ancient times to the space age across a world map.

sources.note: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle: official page
Civilization IV: Steam: released Oct 25 2005; turn-based 4X civilization building on a 3D world (ancient-to-space span not explicit on page)

options.game: Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun
options.how: Five assassins with unique skills sneak through one map, watching guard view cones.
Manage a nation's population, economy and politics from 1836 into the 20th century.

sources.note: Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun: Steam: released Dec 6 2016; five specialists (Hayato, Mugen, Aiko, Yuki, Takuma) with unique skills (view cones not stated)
Victoria II: Steam: released Aug 30 2010; pops, 50+ goods economy, dozens of government types; spans 1835 to the onset of WWII

options.how: Fast unit control (splitting, focus fire, kiting) decides fights alongside intense macro.
Real time with pause: fleets fight automatically, and the decisions are economy, research and empire.

sources.note: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty: official page
Stellaris: Steam: released May 9 2016; tagged Real-Time with Pause; empire building, research, customizable war fleets (auto-resolved fights not stated)

options.how: Up to three heroes with growing special abilities, plus upkeep that punishes big armies, put the emphasis on micromanagement.
Production chains, population needs and trade networks are the core decisions; fights are not where the game is won.

sources.note: Warcraft III: heroes with special abilities; upkeep makes winning by numbers hard, emphasizing micromanagement
Anno 1800: complex production chains, population needs and trading networks

options.how: Small unit selection limits and fast units reward precise control like muta stacking.
Huge armies, strategic zoom and order queues shift focus to economy and production.

sources.note: StarCraft: Brood War: official page
Supreme Commander: official page

options.how: No base building; a few squads with cover, retreat and abilities need constant attention.
Streaming metal and energy economy, queued orders and large armies favor production.

sources.note: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II: official page
Total Annihilation: Released Sep 30 1997; two resources metal and energy balanced as flow, factories queue unlimited complex build orders

options.how: Squads must be moved into cover and pulled back by hand; positioning each squad decides whether it survives a fight.
No direct unit control; you place bounties and buildings, and heroes act on their own.

sources.note: Company of Heroes: review: squads last much longer attacking from behind cover
Majesty: The Fantasy Kingdom Sim: GOG reviews: no direct control of heroes; bounties and flags direct them; guild buildings. GOG date field shows 2001-03-23, original US release was 2000

options.how: Terran, Zerg and Protoss have different units, building and economy rules.
Civilizations share one core tech tree and unit roster, differing in bonuses and a unique unit.

sources.note: StarCraft: Brood War: official page
Age of Empires II: official page

options.how: All armies field the same land, air and naval units; each Commanding Officer only shifts unit strengths and adds a CO Power.
Factions break core rules: the Broken Lords cannot use Food at all and grow population and heal units by spending Dust.

sources.note: Advance Wars: land, air and naval units; Commanding Officers have their own strengths, weaknesses and CO Powers
Endless Legend: Broken Lords cannot use Food and grow population by spending Dust; Dust Care healing

options.how: Marines and aliens play differently: each team has a Commander, but alien players evolve into lifeforms such as wall-running Skulks.
Arm and Core field near-equivalent unit sets that differ mostly in looks and small stat trade-offs.

sources.note: Natural Selection 2: two unique sides, a Commander per team, aliens evolve into five lifeforms
Total Annihilation: Arm and Core are aesthetically different with a similar set of units
Total Annihilation: Arm versus Core store page

options.how: Each faction has its own rules: the Vagabond plays solo and scores by aiding or fighting other factions while managing a pack of items.
No faction differences: every player draws on the same 400-plus technology tree and builds units with the same design system.

sources.note: Root: asymmetrical woodland warfare; the Vagabond scores by improving relations or removing hostile warriors
Warzone 2100: over 400 technologies and a flexible unit design system

options.how: GDI relies on heavy armor and airstrikes, Nod on stealth, speed and cheap units.
All sides use the same research tree and design units from shared parts.

sources.note: Command & Conquer: official page
Warzone 2100: Released Apr 1999; 400+ technology research tree and vehicle design system

options.game: Heroes of Might and Magic III
options.how: Each town type has its own unique buildings and creature line, so every faction builds and fights differently.
Every faction's units match in cost and stats behind different sprites; commanders differ only by their Groove power.

sources.note: Heroes of Might and Magic III: buildings unique to each town type; each town has its own creatures
Wargroove: faction units match in cost and stats with distinct sprites; commanders carry a unique Groove
Wargroove: each commander has a unique special ability, the groove

options.how: Win by conquest, domination, space race, culture, diplomatic vote or score.
Skirmish is won by destroying the enemy base and forces.

sources.note: Civilization IV: Official site: Conquest, Cultural, Diplomatic, Domination, Space Race victories, else points at 2050
Command & Conquer: Red Alert: official page

options.how: Six victory types (science, economy, conquest, wonder, score and supremacy) can be toggled at setup, each suiting different factions.

sources.note: Endless Space 2: several victory paths suited to different factions
Total War: Shogun 2: become Shogun by capturing and holding Kyoto; capture and hold 25, 40 or 60 provinces

options.how: Win by conquest, fame, lore (wisdom), trade or devotion to the gods, plus map-specific objectives.
Melee games end when an opponent's buildings are destroyed.

sources.note: Northgard: Steam lists conquest, fame, lore or trade victory plus devotion to the gods; names differ from claim
Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos: official page

options.how: Victory by military conquest, cultural influence, technological ascension or political alliance.
Skirmish is won by assassination of the enemy commander or annihilation.

sources.note: Galactic Civilizations III: Released May 2015; Steam lists military conquest, cultural domination, technological ascension and political alliance
Supreme Commander: official page

options.how: Win by military conquest (destroy every enemy landmark) or by religion (hold all Sacred Sites for 10 minutes).
Win by defeating the enemy commander or capturing their stronghold.

sources.note: Age of Empires IV: conquest by destroying landmarks; religious victory by holding all Sacred Sites for 10 minutes
Wargroove: goal is to defeat the opposing commander or take their fortress

options.how: Several victory conditions beyond conquest (diplomatic, economic, Transcendence) backed by faction diplomacy.
Skirmish is won by destroying the enemy bases and army; there is no other route to victory.

sources.note: Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri: store page notes multiple victory conditions and a diplomacy system
Halo Wars: official page

options.how: Treaties, trade, alliances and a Galactic Council that votes for a leader.
Every other actor is the zombie horde; there is no one to negotiate with.

sources.note: Master of Orion II: Battle at Antares: GOG: 1996, advanced diplomacy, tributes, comprehensive diplomacy system (Galactic Council not stated on page)
They Are Billions: Full release Jun 18 2019 (early access 2017); enemies are swarms of infected, no diplomacy mentioned

GDI and Nod fight with no negotiation layer; every other side is an enemy.

sources.note: Galactic Civilizations III: Steam: negotiate trade and treaties with rival civilizations (tech trading and opinion tracking not stated)
Command & Conquer: official page

options.how: Diplomacy with nations and tribes, plus marriages and family opinions inside your court.
Waves of enemies attack your towers; there is no diplomacy at all.

Kingdom Rush: Steam: defend with towers and spells against hordes of enemies, no diplomacy mentioned; Steam date is 2014 PC port, 2011 original not stated on page

options.how: Rival rulers can be courted with cunning alliances instead of conquered; diplomacy is a full path to glory.
UNSC battles the Covenant; there is no diplomatic layer.

sources.note: Age of Wonders 4: glory through brutal domination or cunning alliances
Halo Wars: Steam (Definitive Ed. 2017): RTS armies in the Covenant vs UNSC war, no diplomacy mentioned; 2009 original not stated on page

options.how: Marketplace trade, diplomacy with rival empires and assimilating minor factions sit alongside war.
Battles are fought by a few upgradable squads against enemy forces; there is no diplomacy layer.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II: lead and develop squads against the enemies of the Emperor
